scope_label: quality-related spending to evaluate conformity or performance
definition: An appraisal cost is a cost incurred to measure, inspect, test, or audit whether products, services, or processes meet relevant quality requirements.
explanation: It pays for obtaining and evaluating evidence of conformity, such as a product inspection or process audit. Finding a defect is not the same as preventing it.
In cost-of-quality accounting, appraisal is distinct from prevention and from the costs of correcting failures. Where one activity serves several purposes, the accounting boundary should be stated.
